subject.title: [Feature] Re-enable dev channel distribution tag for npm releases

question: Should npm `dev` be retired in favor of git-based moving-main development installs plus npm `alpha`, or preserved as a compatibility dist-tag?
rationale: Current code and the registry implement alpha while public documentation still reserves optional npm dev behavior; implementation evidence cannot determine the intended public compatibility and supply-chain contract.

options.title: Canonicalize git dev plus alpha
options.body: Keep `openclaw update --channel dev` as the moving-main git path, make `alpha` the npm prerelease channel, and remove unsupported npm-dev promises from documentation.

options.title: Add a dev compatibility alias
options.body: Point `dev` at approved alpha or snapshot releases using trusted dist-tag mutation, post-publish verification, and a documented support or removal lifecycle.

options.title: Support distinct alpha and dev channels
options.body: Define separate audiences, versioning, cadence, triggers, updater behavior, provenance, and security gates before implementing both.

recommendation.title: Canonicalize git dev plus alpha
recommendation.body: Keep `openclaw update --channel dev` as the moving-main git path, make `alpha` the npm prerelease channel, and remove unsupported npm-dev promises from documentation.

likelyOwner.reason: Current release-path blame and the existing issue analysis provide the strongest individual routing signal, while CODEOWNERS confirms the decision belongs to release management.
